title: Dominion of Newfoundland
capsule: The Dominion of Newfoundland was a self-governing British dominion comprising the island of Newfoundland and Labrador, formally recognized as a dominion in 1907 and confirmed with full constitutional autonomy under the Statute of Westminster in 1931. Severe debt from World War I mobilization, combined with the Great Depression, made the dominion insolvent by 1932; a royal commission under Lord Amulree recommended and the Newfoundland parliament accepted the suspension of self-government, and the British Parliament passed the Newfoundland Act 1933 establishing a six-member appointed Commission of Government — the only dominion to relinquish its constitutional status. A two-stage referendum in 1948 produced a narrow 52–48 majority for confederation with Canada, and Newfoundland became Canada's tenth province on 31 March 1949 under Premier Joseph Smallwood. The dataset attestation end of 1935 corresponds to the Commission of Government period, when Newfoundland remained a dominion in name but without elected institutions.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Newfoundland's territorial boundaries (the island plus Labrador, the latter's border settled by the Privy Council in 1927) are clearly defined; the political history is fully documented in British and Canadian parliamentary records.
